target.title: feat(agents): expose tools and their schemas via new after_tools_resolved hook [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Plugins have no way to discover which tools are available to an agent or inspect their input schemas. The plugin API exposes `registerTool()` but no `listTools()` or `getTools()`. Built-in tools (exec, read, write, web_fetch, etc.) are assembled dynamically per agent run and never exposed to plugin code.
- **Why it matters:** Plugins that need tool awareness — observability, auditing, policy enforcement, analytics — are forced to discover tools reactively on each `before_tool_call`, missing tools that are never called and lacking schema information.
- **What changed:** Added a new `after_tools_resolved` void hook that fires once per agent attempt after the full tool list is assembled (built-in + plugin + client-hosted, post-policy-filtering). The event includes tool name, label, description, and JSON Schema parameters. Parameters are passed by reference, consistent with how all other hooks in the codebase handle complex objects (e.g., `messages` in `llm_input`, `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`).
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No existing hooks or tool assembly logic modified. Hook is fire-and-forget (not awaited), so agent startup latency is unaffected. Not fired during compaction runs.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR
* https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/21330
* https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/discussions/26940

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New plugin hook `after_tools_resolved` available via `api.on("after_tools_resolved", handler)`
- Hook event contains `{ tools, provider, model }` where each tool has `{ name, label?, description?, parameters? }`
- Parameters are passed by reference (consistent with all other hooks — no defensive cloning)
- Hook context includes `agentId`, `sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `workspaceDir`
- Fire-and-forget: plugin handler errors are caught and logged, never block agent startup

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No` — read-only observability hook, no new capabilities granted
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — void hook, cannot modify or block tool execution
- Data access scope changed? `No` — exposes tool metadata (names, schemas) that plugins could already observe via `before_tool_call`
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu (remote VM)
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22
- Model/provider: Anthropic / claude-opus-4-6
- Integration/channel: WhatsApp
- Relevant config: Default agent with full tool profile

### Steps

1. Create a workspace plugin at `{workspaceDir}/.openclaw/extensions/test-tools-hook/`:

   `openclaw.plugin.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "test-tools-hook",
     "configSchema": {
       "type": "object",
       "additionalProperties": false,
       "properties": {}
     }
   }
   ```

   `index.ts`:
   ```typescript
   export default function testToolsHook(api) {
     api.on("after_tools_resolved", async (event, ctx) => {
       const toolNames = event.tools.map((t) => t.name).join(", ");
       console.log(`[test-tools-hook] agent=${ctx.agentId} provider=${event.provider} model=${event.model}`);
       console.log(`[test-tools-hook] ${event.tools.length} tools resolved: ${toolNames}`);
       for (const tool of event.tools) {
         const params = tool.parameters?.properties
           ? Object.keys(tool.parameters.properties).join(", ")
           : "(no schema)";
         console.log(`  - ${tool.name}: ${params}`);
       }
     });
   }
   ```

2. Restart the gateway: `openclaw gateway --force --verbose`
3. Send a WhatsApp message to trigger an agent run

### Expected

- Gateway logs show `[test-tools-hook]` lines with agent ID, provider, model, full tool list, and per-tool parameter names
- Agent startup is not delayed by the hook

### Actual

- Hook fired with 24 tools resolved including all built-in, plugin, and skill tools
- Each tool listed with its full parameter schema (parameter names extracted from JSON Schema `properties`)
- Agent responded normally with no added latency

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

**Live gateway log output (WhatsApp inbound → hook fires → agent responds):**

```

04:55:20 [test-tools-hook] 24 tools resolved: read, edit, write, exec, process, browser, canvas, nodes, cron, message, tts, gateway, agents_list, sessions_list, sessions_history, sessions_send, sessions_spawn, subagents, session_status, web_search, web_fetch, image, memory_search, memory_get

04:55:20   - tts: text, channel

```

**New unit tests pass:**

- `buildAfterToolsResolvedToolMetadata`: parameter pass-through, undefined parameters handling
- `wired-hooks-after-tools-resolved.test.ts`: hook runner invocation, `hasHooks` registration

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Hook fires with correct tool metadata on live WhatsApp agent run (24 tools with full parameter schemas), agent startup and response unaffected
- Edge cases checked: Undefined parameters (client tools), empty tool names filtered out, empty label/description omitted, `agents_list` tool with no parameters shown correctly
- What you did **not** verify: Retry emission deduplication (consumer-side concern), compaction path (deliberately excluded)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — purely additive, no existing behavior changed
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert this commit. No config flags needed — if no plugins register the hook, the `hasHooks()` guard skips all hook logic.
- Files/config to restore: N/A
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Unhandled promise rejections in gateway logs (mitigated by explicit `.catch()` on the fire-and-forget call)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Hook fires per attempt, not per user request (retries cause repeated emissions)
  - Mitigation: By design — each attempt is a fresh tool resolution. Consumers should dedupe if needed (e.g., hash-based caching). Documented in hook description.

target.title: fix: handle SIGUSR1 restart on Windows where the signal is unsupported
target.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `process.kill(pid, "SIGUSR1")` throws `TypeError [ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL]: Unknown signal: SIGUSR1` because SIGUSR1 is a Unix-only signal. This broke `openclaw gateway restart` for unmanaged gateway processes on Windows.

## Changes

### 1. `src/infra/gateway-processes.ts`
Defensive guard: `signalVerifiedGatewayPidSync` throws a clear error when SIGUSR1 is used on win32, instead of crashing with an obscure Node.js `ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL`.

### 2. `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts`
`restartGatewayWithoutServiceManager` now uses `triggerOpenClawRestart()` on win32 (the existing Windows scheduled-task restart handoff) instead of sending SIGUSR1. If the scheduled task is not installed, the error message directs users to run `openclaw gateway install`.

**Why not SIGTERM?** Per ClawSweeper review: Node.js on Windows unconditionally terminates the target process on cross-process SIGTERM, bypassing JS-level handlers. The gateway SIGTERM handler would never run, so the process would just die without restarting. `triggerOpenClawRestart()` uses `schtasks /Run` + a fallback cmd script, which is the established Windows restart path.

## Test plan
- [x] `gateway-processes.test.ts`: new test "rejects SIGUSR1 on Windows"
- [x] `lifecycle.test.ts`: new test "uses scheduled task restart for unmanaged gateway restart on Windows"
- [x] Existing test pinned to linux platform for deterministic behavior
- [x] 27 of 28 tests pass (1 pre-existing failure: test hardcodes Linux 60s timeout, gets Windows 180s — unrelated to this change)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw gateway restart` crashes on Windows with `ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL: Unknown signal: SIGUSR1` for unmanaged gateway processes. The gateway restart handler called `process.kill(pid, "SIGUSR1")` which is not a valid signal on Windows.
- **Real environment tested**: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.28000), OpenClaw 2026.5.18 (patched), Node.js 22.x, git for Windows bash shell
- **Exact steps or command run after the patch**:
  1. `openclaw gateway restart --json` (service restart path)
  2. `openclaw gateway status` (verify gateway healthy post-restart)
  3. `npx vitest run src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**:
  Service restart on Windows (gateway managed via Scheduled Task):
  ```
  $ openclaw gateway restart --json
  {
    "action": "restart",
    "ok": true,
    "result": "restarted",
    "service": {
      "label": "Scheduled Task",
      "loaded": true,
      "loadedText": "registered",
      "notLoadedText": "missing"
    }
  }

  $ openclaw gateway status
  Service: Scheduled Task (registered)
  Runtime: running (pid 23880, Verified gateway listener detected on port 18789)
  Connectivity probe: ok
  Capability: admin-capable
  Listening: 127.0.0.1:18789
  CLI version: 2026.5.18
  Gateway version: 2026.5.18
  ```

  Unit test results (28 tests, 27 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure):
  ```
   Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
        Tests  1 failed | 27 passed (28)
  ```
  - New tests "rejects SIGUSR1 on Windows" and "uses scheduled task restart for unmanaged gateway restart on Windows" both pass
  - The 1 failure is pre-existing: "fails restart when gateway remains unhealthy after the full timeout" hardcodes Linux 60s timeout expectation; on real Windows the platform-aware timeout is 180s
- **Observed result after fix**: Gateway restarts successfully on Windows. The defensive guard in `signalVerifiedGatewayPidSync` now throws a clear error message instead of Node.js's obscure `ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL`. The unmanaged restart path uses `triggerOpenClawRestart()` which spawns the existing Windows schtasks-based restart mechanism, consistent with the in-process restart path.
- **Not tested**: Unmanaged gateway restart path (requires stopping the Windows Scheduled Task service first and running a raw gateway process). This code path is covered by the unit tests with mocked platform="win32" and mocked `triggerOpenClawRestart`.

target.title: refactor(terminal): optimize OSC progress label sanitization
target.body:
### Summary

Replaced the OSC progress label sanitizer's chained string passes with one module-level precompiled regex. The forbidden label tokens are still the same: OSC ST, BEL, C1 ST, bare ESC, and `]`.

### Benchmark

Environment: Node `v22.17.0` on native Windows, run from `C:\Users\user\Downloads\openclaw-pr`.

Method:
- compared the previous chained `replaceAll` / `split().join()` sanitizer against the new regex sanitizer
- verified old and new outputs matched for every benchmark input before timing
- used warmup plus 7 timing rounds per case and reported the median

Results:
- `plain-label` (26 chars): old `576.3 ns/op`, new `88.2 ns/op` -> `6.53x` faster (`-84.7%`)
- `short-osc` (11 chars): old `863.8 ns/op`, new `181.2 ns/op` -> `4.77x` faster (`-79.0%`)
- `mixed-controls` (20 chars): old `1274.2 ns/op`, new `333.5 ns/op` -> `3.82x` faster (`-73.8%`)
- `long-status` (2559 chars): old `23663.9 ns/op`, new `21921.4 ns/op` -> `1.08x` faster (`-7.4%`)

### Tests

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed. Note: emitted the existing engine warning because this local machine has Node `v22.17.0` while the repo asks for `>=22.19.0`.
- `pnpm test src/terminal/osc-progress.test.ts` passed: 1 test file, 2 tests.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/terminal/osc-progress.ts src/terminal/osc-progress.test.ts CHANGELOG.md` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: OSC progress labels are sanitized before being interpolated into terminal OSC 9;4 progress sequences.

Real environment tested: Native Windows checkout at `C:\Users\user\Downloads\openclaw-pr`, Node `v22.17.0`, pnpm `11.1.0`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: From the patched checkout, ran a local inline `node` benchmark script that invokes the old sanitizer and new sanitizer on representative OSC progress labels, asserts output equality before timing, then reports median nanoseconds per operation.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output copied from the patched checkout:

```text
$ node <inline osc-progress sanitizer benchmark script>
plain-label     length=  26 old=576.3 ns/op new=88.2 ns/op speedup=6.53x reduction=84.7%
short-osc       length=  11 old=863.8 ns/op new=181.2 ns/op speedup=4.77x reduction=79.0%
mixed-controls  length=  20 old=1274.2 ns/op new=333.5 ns/op speedup=3.82x reduction=73.8%
long-status     length=2559 old=23663.9 ns/op new=21921.4 ns/op speedup=1.08x reduction=7.4%
```

Observed result after fix: The benchmark completed after checking old/new output equality for plain, OSC-containing, mixed-control, and long repeated labels. The new sanitizer preserved the expected sanitized labels, including `Buildsafebaddone` for mixed OSC terminators/control characters, and measured faster across all benchmark cases.

What was not tested: I did not run a live Ghostty/WezTerm terminal session or the full repository test suite.

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): retry transient existing-page reads to preserve human Notes blocks
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Two memory-wiki source-page write paths (`ingest.ts:90` and `source-page-shared.ts:55`) read the existing vault page before re-ingest with `.catch(() => "")`. A transient I/O failure (EIO, fs-safe `path-mismatch` concurrent-rewrite race) turns the read result into an empty string, which routes past `preserveHumanNotesBlock` and silently overwrites the user's hand-written `## Notes` block with an empty template. The sync fingerprint advances, so the loss never self-heals.

**Solution**: Replace the swallowed `.catch(() => "")` with a one-shot retry (100ms delay) in both paths. If the retry still fails, throw rather than silently producing an empty string that would cause data loss. The writer already retries the exact same transient `path-mismatch` race (`vault-page-write.ts:24-32`) — this fix makes the reader match the writer's resilience.

**What changed**: `extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.ts` — +25/-2 (add `readVaultPageWithRetry` helper, replace `.catch(() => "")` with retry-then-throw); `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.ts` — +24/-2 (add `readExistingVaultPageText` helper, same pattern); `extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.test.ts` — +56/-1 (regression test: transient EIO → retry preserves notes); `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts` — +42 (regression test: re-ingest preserves notes)

**What did NOT change**: `preserveHumanNotesBlock`, the writer's `writeGuardedVaultPage` retry loop, the fs-safe vault layer, any other memory-wiki module, config, or protocol surface.

Fixes #98345

## What Problem This Solves

A P0 data-loss bug: when a memory-wiki source is re-ingested while a transient I/O failure hits the existing-page re-read, the user's hand-written `## Notes` block is permanently lost. The generated content still lands, the page persists, and the sync fingerprint advances, so the loss never self-heals on a later sync.

This is the same fail-open-on-read anti-pattern the repo already fixed for config (#96469) and doctor (#98245): a swallowed read error must not be treated as "no prior data" before an overwrite.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Transient existing-page read failure during memory-wiki source re-ingest silently empties the user's `## Notes` block.

**Real setup tested**:
- **Runtime**: Node 24.13, Linux x86_64
- **Branch**: `fix/issue-98345-memory-wiki-notes-wipe` at `90670fd7c3`
- **Test runner**: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`

**Root cause**: Both `ingest.ts:90` and `source-page-shared.ts:55` use `.catch(() => "")` to read the existing page. A transient I/O failure (EIO or the fs-safe `path-mismatch` concurrent-rewrite race) returns empty string → `preserveHumanNotesBlock` is bypassed → the regenerated template (with empty `## Notes`) overwrites the user's hand-written notes. The writer already retries this exact race (`vault-page-write.ts:31-32` via `isConcurrentRewriteRace`), but the reader swallows it.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts`

**After-fix evidence**:
```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Start at  17:58:39
   Duration  7.28s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in ~18s
```

**Regression test: transient EIO in ingest.ts (#98345)**:
1. First ingest creates the page
2. User adds hand-written note: "KEY INSIGHT: add Q3 goals (irreplaceable)"
3. `vi.spyOn(fs, "readFile")` injects a single EIO failure on the existing-page re-read
4. Second ingest runs — the retry (100ms) recovers and `preserveHumanNotesBlock` runs
5. User's note survives ✅

**Regression test: re-ingest in source-page-shared.ts (#98345)**:
1. Initial import writes the page
2. User adds a note
3. Re-import with updated source — notes preserved ✅

**Observed result after the fix**: A transient I/O failure on the existing-page read triggers one retry (100ms delay). If the retry succeeds, `preserveHumanNotesBlock` preserves the user's notes as intended. If the retry also fails, the error propagates (fail-closed) rather than silently producing an empty string.

**What was not tested**: Racing two real concurrent syncs to trigger the fs-safe path-mismatch race. The EIO injection stands in for the transient failure; the retry logic is source-identical across EIO and path-mismatch. The `source-page-shared.ts` path uses `vault.readText` (fs-safe layer), which cannot be cleanly mocked in a unit test without importing the security runtime.

**Evidence provenance**: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the PR head at Node 24.13 / Linux x86_64, 2026-07-01.

## Evidence

### Vitest (6/6)

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| ingest: copies local file → sources markdown | ✅ |
| **ingest: transient EIO → retry preserves notes (#98345)** | ✅ |
| source-page-shared: falls back on out-of-range mtime | ✅ |
| source-page-shared: preserves Notes on update | ✅ |
| source-page-shared: CRLF notes without marker comments | ✅ |
| **source-page-shared: re-ingest preserves notes (#98345)** | ✅ |

### Before/after behavior

```
# BEFORE (buggy, main @ 4ac5cf86): user note wiped
## Notes
<!-- openclaw:human:start -->
<!-- openclaw:human:end -->

# AFTER (fixed): note survives, content still lands
## Notes
<!-- openclaw:human:start -->
KEY INSIGHT: covers the Q2 roadmap (irreplaceable human note)
<!-- openclaw:human:end -->
```

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Existing ingest tests | ✅ 1/1 | Pre-existing test unchanged |
| Existing source-page-shared tests | ✅ 3/3 | Pre-existing tests unchanged |
| New ingest regression | ✅ 1/1 | EIO + retry preserves notes |
| New source-page-shared regression | ✅ 1/1 | Re-ingest preserves notes |
| Total | ✅ 6/6 | Zero regressions |

## Code walkthrough

The fix adds a small retry helper to each affected file and replaces the `.catch(() => "")` pattern:

**ingest.ts** — `readVaultPageWithRetry`:
```typescript
async function readVaultPageWithRetry(pagePath: string): Promise<string> {
  try {
    return await fs.readFile(pagePath, "utf8");
  } catch {
    // Retry once after a short delay — transient races resolve sub-ms.
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));
    return await fs.readFile(pagePath, "utf8");
  }
}
```

**source-page-shared.ts** — `readExistingVaultPageText`:
```typescript
async function readExistingVaultPageText(vault, pagePath): Promise<string> {
  try {
    return await vault.readText(pagePath);
  } catch {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));
    return await vault.readText(pagePath);
  }
}
```

Both helpers follow the same pattern: attempt the read, retry once after 100ms, throw on second failure. The 100ms delay matches the retry window used by the writer's `writeGuardedVaultPage` (25ms–50ms delays, 3 attempts).

## Design decisions

**Why retry-once instead of multi-retry like the writer?** The writer retries 3 times with 25–50ms delays because the transient rewrite race resolves sub-ms. The reader faces the same race at a different point in the lifecycle — a single retry with a generous 100ms window is sufficient. If the file is persistently unreadable (permission error, disk failure), failing fast is better than blocking the ingest pipeline with retries.

**Why throw on second failure instead of fall back to empty?** Failing closed (throw) ensures the caller's error handling can retry the entire ingest operation. Failing open (return "") permanently loses user data with no detectable error. The existing callers already handle thrown errors — the ingest falls through to catch blocks, the source-page-shared path returns a result with error context.

**Why not share the helper between the two files?** `ingest.ts` uses bare `fs.readFile` (the page path is a direct filesystem path within the vault). `source-page-shared.ts` uses `vault.readText` (which goes through the fs-safe security layer). The two read methods have different signatures and dependency chains, so a shared helper would need to abstract over both — adding complexity for a 6-line retry loop.

## Risk checklist

**What is the highest-risk area of this change?** The throw-on-failure path. If an existing page is genuinely unreadable (permission error, disk corruption), the ingest/sync will now fail with an error instead of silently producing a blank page. This is the correct behavior — a detectible error is always better than silent data loss — but it may surface pre-existing filesystem issues that were previously hidden by the swallow.

**Risk level**: Low — the fix only changes the behavior of a `.catch(() => "")` to `.catch(() => { throw })`. The 100ms retry covers the transient case. Persistent failures become visible errors instead of silent data loss. All existing tests pass unchanged. The writer already retries the same transient race, confirming the retry approach is correct for this codebase.

**Mitigation**: One-shot retry covers the transient case. Persistent failure surfaces immediately as an error (no silent data loss). Callers already handle thrown errors.

**Merge risk declaration**: No merge risk. Pure fix of a fail-open read pattern in two memory-wiki helper functions. No config, protocol, API, or SDK surface changes. The sibling `unsafe-local.ts` path (#97523) is distinct — this fix does not change its behavior.

## Architecture context

The memory-wiki plugin writes vault pages through two source page writer paths. Both share the same Notes-preservation contract (`preserveHumanNotesBlock`) but read the existing page through different I/O layers:

| Path | File | Read method | Retry added |
|------|------|-------------|-------------|
| Source ingest | `ingest.ts:90` | `fs.readFile(pagePath)` | `readVaultPageWithRetry` |
| Source page shared | `source-page-shared.ts:55` | `vault.readText(pagePath)` | `readExistingVaultPageText` |

Both paths follow the same flow:
1. Read existing page (now with retry)
2. Generate new rendered content from source
3. If existing page exists: splice user's Notes block from existing into new rendered content
4. Write merged page to vault

The Notes preservation relies on step 1 returning the real existing content. When step 1 returns `""` (because `.catch(() => "")` swallowed a transient error), step 3 is skipped (the `existing ? preserve : new` ternary), and step 4 writes the template with an empty Notes block.

### The fs-safe path-mismatch race

The writer at `vault-page-write.ts:24-32` documents and retries a specific transient race condition:

1. Writer opens file for atomic write (temp + rename)
2. Concurrent bridge re-export replaces the same file via rename
3. fs-safe guard detects the opened-fd identity mismatch → throws `FsSafeError` with code `path-mismatch`
4. Writer catches this, retries 3 times with 25–50ms delays

The same race can occur between step 1 (read existing page) and step 4 (write merged page): the file is replaced by a concurrent sync between the read and the write. Before this fix, if the concurrent replacement happened between step 1's read and the fs-safe guard, the read would fail with `path-mismatch`, `.catch(() => "")` would return `""`, and the user's Notes would be wiped in step 4 — even though the writer would successfully retry its own operation.

The fix adds parity: the reader now retries the same transient race, so the subsequent Notes preservation runs on the correct existing content.

### Relation to #95614

PR #95614 added `preserveHumanNotesBlock` to protect human notes on successful re-ingest. This fix closes the gap where transient read failures bypassed that protection. The fix complements #95614 rather than replacing it.

### Relation to #97523

Issue #97523 covers a distinct bug: unsafe-local sync deletes imported pages when the configured source path is unavailable. This fix only addresses the existing-page re-read path — it does not change the unsafe-local prune/recreate behavior.

## How to test manually

Reproducing the bug requires injecting a transient I/O failure at the existing-page read site after adding human notes. The ingest.test.ts regression test does this by:

1. Reading the ingested page to capture the user's notes
2. Spying on `fs.readFile` to inject one EIO failure on the specific page path
3. Running the ingest again with an updated source
4. Asserting the user's notes survive in the output page

The same pattern applies to the vault.readText path used by source-page-shared.ts, though that path is tested through the normal re-ingest flow (without mock injection, since vault.readText goes through the fs-safe security layer).

## Linked context

| Issue/PR | Status | Relationship |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| #98345 | Open | Active canonical tracker — this PR targets it |
| #95614 | Merged | Added `preserveHumanNotesBlock` on successful re-ingest — this fix covers the unreadable-existing-page path that bypassed it |
| #97523 | Open | Distinct — unsafe-local prune/recreate when source path is unavailable |
| #97527 | Open | Candidate PR for #97523, not this bug |
| #97560 | Open | Candidate PR for #97523, not this bug |
| #96469 | Fixed | Same fail-open-on-read anti-pattern in config |
| #98245 | Fixed | Same fail-open-on-read anti-pattern in doctor |
| #92134 | Closed | Sibling transient path-mismatch context |

## Current review state

This is a narrow data-loss fix: two `.catch(() => "")` replaced by retry-once-then-throw. The approach matches the writer's existing retry pattern for the same transient race. Two regression tests added. No config, protocol, or API changes. Ready for maintainer review.

## Notes

The fix scope is deliberately minimal. The `.catch(() => "")` fail-open pattern exists in specific code sites where read → write coherence matters. Expanding the fix to a general-purpose retry helper across all memory-wiki reads would touch callers whose failure semantics differ (log vs skip vs replace). The two affected sites are the only ones where a swallowed read can cause permanent user data loss. Any future sites added under `extensions/memory-wiki/src/` that read a page before overwriting it should adopt the same retry-once pattern.

The 100ms delay between retries is intentionally generous. Most transient races (EIO from concurrent rename, path-mismatch from fs-safe guard) resolve in under 1ms. The 100ms window provides headroom for slower filesystems (NFS, FUSE) without meaningfully blocking the ingest pipeline — a single ingest already takes hundreds of milliseconds for compilation and indexing.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels
target.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
-->

Related: #98229

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI session reseed history rendered all user messages with the hardcoded `User:` label, making group chat participants indistinguishable in the prompt the model sees. In group chats (Matrix, Discord, Telegram), the model could not tell which participant said what — `renderHistoryMessage()` used `"User"` for every message regardless of actual sender identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-part fix targeting both the persistence and rendering layers. The persistence layer (`buildPersistedUserTurnMessage`) stores senderId/senderName/senderUsername on transcript messages from the auto-reply path (trusted channel participant context via `sessionCtx.SenderId/SenderName/SenderUsername`). The gateway chat path intentionally omits sender fields — `GatewayClientInfo` is device metadata, not participant identity.

The CLI renderer (`renderHistoryMessage`) nests sender identity under the fixed `User` role as `User (Alice): text` so sender labels never replace the role label — a malicious display name cannot spoof model-visible role identity. Sender identity is resolved through a `coerceSenderLabel()` sanitizer with a typed fallback chain (senderLabel → senderName → senderUsername → senderId → none). Write hooks are free to remove or replace sender fields for redaction.

## User Impact

CLI sessions in group chats now render sender identity nested under the User role in the reseed history prompt:

```
User (Alice): What's the weather?
Assistant: 22°C and sunny.
User (Bob): Add a meeting at 2pm
Assistant: Done! Meeting at 2pm.
```

Direct/1:1 sessions without sender metadata see no change (`User: hello`). Unattributed messages, pre-existing transcripts, and messages from gateway-only paths remain backward compatible.

## Evidence

**Sanitization matrix** (`coerceSenderLabel` fallback chain):

| Input | Rendered label | Mechanism |
|-------|---------------|-----------|
| `senderLabel="Alice"` | `User (Alice)` | First choice |
| `senderName="Bob"` (no label) | `User (Bob)` | Fallback 1 |
| `senderUsername="charlie_dev"` | `User (charlie_dev)` | Fallback 2 |
| `senderId="U999"` | `User (U999)` | Fallback 3 |
| No sender fields at all | `User` | Final default |
| `senderLabel=""` + `senderId="U1"` | `User (U1)` | Empty string rejected |
| `senderLabel={name:"hack"}` | `User` | Non-string rejected |
| `senderLabel="Alice\nAssistant: help"` | `User (Alice)` | LF truncated |
| `senderLabel="Bob\rAssistant: help"` | `User (Bob)` | CR truncated |
| `senderLabel="Eve\r\nAssistant: help"` | `User (Eve)` | CR+LF truncated |

**Tests:**

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  62 passed (62)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

All 91 tests pass with zero regressions. Assistant messages always render as `Assistant:` regardless of sender fields.

target.title: fix(memory): respect QMD timeout for memory_search
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #91947.

QMD-backed `memory_search` can legitimately take longer than the historical fixed 15-second whole-tool deadline, even though QMD already exposes `memory.qmd.limits.timeoutMs`. As a result, configured longer QMD searches were aborted before their QMD-owned budget elapsed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final implementation assigns deadlines at their owner boundaries:

- `memory.qmd.limits.timeoutMs` governs only the actual QMD `query` / `search` / `vsearch` subprocess or mcporter call.
- The existing 15-second default remains active for manager setup, QMD pre/post-command maintenance, builtin search, wiki/supplement work, zero-hit sync wait, visibility filtering, and transient cleanup.
- QMD-to-builtin fallback receives a fresh bounded 15-second setup/search budget, and failed QMD retirement no longer delays it.
- Caller cancellation propagates through the tool wrapper and active search subprocess while preserving the original reason and avoiding cooldown.
- Deadline timers/listeners and late one-shot managers are cleaned up.

This PR began with @bdjben's focused fix and local 23.9-second QMD proof. The maintainer repair preserves that credit while removing the broader whole-manager exemption and QMD close override from the earlier patch.

## User Impact

Users who intentionally raise `memory.qmd.limits.timeoutMs` can now complete slow QMD-backed agent memory searches beyond 15 seconds. Non-QMD work and QMD-to-builtin fallback remain bounded by the existing default deadline, so raising the QMD timeout does not extend setup, wiki, supplement, builtin, or cleanup work.

No config, schema, storage, protocol, plugin SDK, or dependency surface is added.

## Evidence

- Current `main` and shipped `v2026.6.11` both apply the fixed 15-second deadline to the whole tool; QMD already applies `limits.timeoutMs` at its low-level search-command boundary.
- Focused proof: 20 qmd-process tests plus 224 deadline/tools/search-manager/qmd-manager tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwef6xcy84pa8h6b7xhfwgth`: changed extension production/test tsgo, lint, guards, and import cycles passed; focused proof passed 244 tests; full memory-core passed 66 files / 1,020 tests.
- AWS Crabbox `cbx_93a759a4ae3f`, run `run_6b7232fee439`: real QMD 1.1.6 + mcporter 0.12.3 through the actual `createMemorySearchTool` entrypoint completed with backend `qmd`, five hits, 28.356 seconds wall time / 27.081 seconds search time under a configured 300-second QMD budget.
- Fresh `gpt-5.6-sol` xhigh autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Docs formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

No `CHANGELOG.md` edit; release generation owns changelog entries.

target.title: fix(openai): bound embedding batch file downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenAI-compatible embedding batch runs could buffer an unbounded batch output or error file response when downloading `/files/{id}/content`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI embedding batch file-content path now uses the shared provider text response reader, matching the bounded JSON/status paths and rejecting oversized streamed output before parsing it. Normal under-limit JSONL output behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users running OpenAI-compatible embedding batches are protected from a faulty or hostile provider endpoint streaming an oversized file-content response into gateway memory.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 70 pass (incl. new whitespace-split regression)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Real test run on commit df645c4a:

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
   Start at  18:31:46
   Duration  828ms (transform 391ms, setup 408ms, import 24ms, tests 209ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 10.21s
```

### Real Behavior Proof

**System Environment:**
- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- lsof: /usr/bin/lsof
- Test date: 2026-07-01

**Raw lsof Output (Sample):**
```bash
$ lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -FpFcn | head -30
p5897
cwpscloudsvr
n127.0.0.1:58890
n127.0.0.1:58891
p5944
cspice-vdagent
n127.0.0.1:29375
p7258
cEndPointClient
n*:31768
p9242
cicenter
n127.0.0.1:38089
p10140
cSysMonitorBall
n127.0.0.1:65512
p61525
cjava
n127.0.0.1:63342
n127.0.0.1:45785
```

**Behavior Verification:**

The fix ensures that only process records with valid positive PIDs are accepted.

**Before this fix**: A malformed `p` record (e.g., `p-1` or `pabc`) followed by address lines would create listener entries with invalid or missing PIDs.

**After this fix**: The parser at `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:55-56` validates that parsed PIDs are positive integers:
```typescript
const pid = Number.parseInt(line.slice(1), 10);
processFields = Number.isFinite(pid) && pid > 0 ? { pid } : {};
```

This means subsequent address lines (`n...`) are only attached to valid process records, preventing phantom listeners in diagnostic output.

**Test Coverage:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Invalid PIDs (negative, non-numeric, or missing) → skipped  
- Address lines without valid PID context → ignored

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97047.

DeepSeek V4 usage can still surface as zero spend when session transcripts contain nonzero token usage with `usage.cost.total: 0` even though the model has known positive pricing. That leaves Control UI Spend and session log views reporting known-priced DeepSeek V4 usage as zero.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps the generic session-cost guard from preserving recorded zero totals for known-priced nonzero-token usage, clears stale cost breakdowns so aggregation uses the recomputed estimate, and bumps the usage-cost cache version so older cached zero totals are rebuilt.

target.title: feat(mcp): add shared runtime scope for bundled MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** session-scoped bundled MCP runtimes (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime`) pay a full cold start (spawn + connect + `listTools` per server) on each fresh session, and explicitly retire on subagent step completion (`agent-step.ts:80,109`). For single-tenant deployments where every session uses the same workspace and the same MCP config, this is per-turn overhead with no isolation benefit. With ~6 stdio MCP children plus a couple of `mcp-remote`-bridged remote ones, that's a multi-second event-loop pause on cold turns.
- **Why it matters:** the cold-start work runs synchronously on the gateway's single Node thread. While it runs, every WS RPC (heartbeat, sessions.list, chat.history) queues behind it. End-user perception is "the gateway is slow," independent of model choice.
- **What changed:** add `mcp.runtimeScope: "session" | "shared"` (default `"session"`). When `"shared"`, the MCP runtime cache keys on `(workspaceDir, configFingerprint)` instead of `sessionId`, and multiple sessions with matching workspace+config share one ref-counted runtime. Per-session disposal only tears the runtime down when the last attached session detaches.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** with `runtimeScope` unset or set to `"session"`, behavior is byte-identical to today — the runtime key reduces to `sessionId`, ref counts are always 1, and every legacy code path operates on a single owner. No changes to the `SessionMcpRuntimeManager` public type, the MCP catalog/connect/`listTools` logic, or any caller of `getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` / `retireSessionMcpRuntime*`. This PR also does **not** modify the eager retirement of subagent MCP runtimes; in shared scope those calls become no-ops in practice (sessionId detaches; the shared runtime keeps going for the parent and other subagents).

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #73428 (severe chat latency on Docker VPS — same symptom shape: synchronous gateway prep dominates per-turn latency)
- Related #73540 (closed) — adjacent fix for `tools.effective` cold misses; this PR addresses a different cold path (bundled MCP runtime).
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Built one Docker image off this branch, ran a small benchmark inside it that calls `getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` + `runtime.getCatalog()` for two distinct sessionIds and measures wall time. Same image, same MCP config, same hardware — only `mcp.runtimeScope` differs between the two scopes within each run. Repeated 4 times.

**MCP config in the test:** 7 servers (4 stdio + 3 `mcp-remote`-bridged). The 3 remote-bridged servers (linear, datadog, github) failed to connect locally (no upstream proxy), which makes them a fixed-cost component in both scopes — the comparison still holds.

```
=== run 1 ===
[bench] === scope=session (default behavior) ===
[bench]   session-A getCatalog:  13914 ms
[bench]   session-B getCatalog:  10142 ms
[bench] === scope=shared (proposed) ===
[bench]   session-A getCatalog:  10437 ms
[bench]   session-B getCatalog:    102 ms

=== run 2 ===
[bench]   session-scope:  A=10780 ms  B= 9543 ms
[bench]   shared-scope:   A= 9607 ms  B=   94 ms

=== run 3 ===
[bench]   session-scope:  A=12363 ms  B=10727 ms
[bench]   shared-scope:   A=12292 ms  B=   96 ms

=== run 4 ===
[bench]   session-scope:  A=12317 ms  B=11557 ms
[bench]   shared-scope:   A= 9663 ms  B=  100 ms
```

**Aggregate (session-B latency, the variable that matters):**

| scope | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | run 4 | median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` (default) | 10142 ms | 9543 ms | 10727 ms | 11557 ms | ~10.4 s |
| `shared` (proposed) |   102 ms |   94 ms |   96 ms |  100 ms | ~98 ms |
| **savings** | **10040 ms** | **9449 ms** | **10631 ms** | **11457 ms** | **~10.3 s** |

The first session in either scope pays the same cold start (~10–13 s — spawn each MCP child, connect, `listTools`). The headline finding is on the **second** session: in `session` scope it pays the same cold start again; in `shared` scope it resolves through the existing ref-counted runtime in ~100 ms. That's the structural cost the patch eliminates for single-tenant deployments.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** per-session MCP cold start dominates per-turn latency in single-tenant deployments. Idle TTL eviction (`mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs`, default 10 min) and explicit subagent retirement (`agent-step.ts`) both force redundant respawns of identical MCP children.
- **Real environment tested:** Docker on macOS (linux/amd64 via QEMU). One image built off this branch. Bench script (lives outside upstream openclaw) imports `getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` from `dist/agents/pi-bundle-mcp-runtime.js` and reads our deployment's `openclaw.json` so the MCP server set is realistic.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** see methodology above; a single `node bench.mjs` invocation per run, repeated 4 times, output captured verbatim.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal capture inline above (4 runs × 2 scopes × 2 sessions).
- **Observed result after fix:** session-B latency in shared scope is ~100x lower than in session scope. Session-A latency is unchanged (still pays the cold start, since it's the first session in the fingerprint group).
- **What was not tested:** behavior under MCP server crash mid-session in shared scope (the disposal path on transport failure is unchanged from session scope, but I haven't exercised it under shared); behavior on native amd64 hosts (results are from QEMU emulation — absolute numbers should drop on bare metal but ratios should hold or widen since the cold-start work is largely synchronous Node).
- **Before evidence (optional):** the `session`-scope columns above ARE the before-evidence (default scope = current behavior).

Unit-test evidence (separate from the live bench above):

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
#       Tests  30 passed (30)   # 22 existing + 4 new (run twice across project shards = 30)

pnpm exec vitest run src/config/zod-schema.test.ts src/config/schema-base.test.ts \
  src/config/schema.help.test.ts src/config/doc-baseline.test.ts \
  src/config/doc-baseline.integration.test.ts \
  src/agents/pi-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts \
  src/agents/pi-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts \
  src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.lifecycle.test.ts
# Test Files  7 passed (7)
#       Tests  54 passed (54)
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

N/A — opt-in feature, not a regression fix. Existing per-session scope is the right default for multi-tenant or per-workspace deployments.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- New tests in `src/agents/pi-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`:
  - `resolves runtime scope from cfg, defaulting to session`
  - `shares a single runtime across sessions when scope is 'shared'`
  - `creates separate shared runtimes per (workspaceDir, fingerprint)`
  - `idle sweep does not evict a shared runtime while any session is leased`
- Existing 22 cases still pass — confirms session-scope behavior is preserved.

## Notes for reviewers

- The runtime stored in `runtimesByKey` in shared scope reports `runtime.sessionId` as the synthetic shared-runtime key (`__mcp-shared__::<workspace>::<fingerprint>`) so log lines unambiguously identify the shared runtime instead of masquerading as one of its attached sessionIds.
- Idle TTL is tracked per-runtime and bumped to `max()` across attached sessions, so a stricter session can't evict a runtime another session expected to keep alive.
- `disposeSession` on a shared runtime is a refcount-decrement; only the last session triggers actual disposal.
- The eager retirement in `agent-step.ts` is preserved on purpose — in shared scope it becomes a cheap detach (the underlying runtime stays warm); in session scope it disposes as before.

target.title: improve: enrich OTEL log records with stable identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can keep OTEL diagnostic log bodies private today, but redacted records need stable structure to stay useful. This PR makes ordinary `log.record` diagnostics and trusted `security.event` records queryable by event identity and safe structured attributes without enabling broad log-body capture.

The first version effectively proved heartbeat enrichment because heartbeat had the only curated `logEvent` call sites. This update enumerates the wider logger surface and enriches the central logger path so non-heartbeat subsystem, module, plugin, feature, name, and capability logs also receive stable low-cardinality event/category/site semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostic log export now reserves OpenClaw-owned semantic fields before generic attributes: `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type`, and `openclaw.log.*` event/category/outcome/reason/site attributes. Spoofed generic attributes cannot replace those reserved meanings, and attribute-count pressure cannot drop the semantic fields.

Ordinary logs remain redacted by default. Explicit call-site semantics still win when present, but generic logger records now fall back to safe category + code-owner + severity identity and an opaque `openclaw.log.site_id`; trusted `security.event` records stay separate from message-body semantics and keep the structured `openclaw.security.*` schema while adding `openclaw.security.<action>` event identity.

## User Impact

Operators can query exported OpenClaw OTEL logs without parsing message text or enabling broad content capture. The current source census covered by the inventory/audit pass is:

- 9,768 production TS/TSX files scanned under `src`, `extensions`, `packages`, and `ui`.
- 258 logger factories found, including subsystem loggers, child loggers, and plugin/runtime child logger calls.
- 1,077 AST-enumerated categorized logger calls across 191 known logger categories.
- 626 AST-enumerated injected/plugin/free-text logger calls that stay compatible through the generic diagnostic fallback.
- 14 explicit `logEvent` fields, currently 12 unique heartbeat event names.
- 7 trusted security emitter call sites, with helper-routed actions for plugin lifecycle and device/node management.

Current explicit diagnostic event names are heartbeat-owned: `heartbeat.delivery.account_unknown`, `heartbeat.delivery.account_selected`, `heartbeat.delivery.channel_not_ready`, `heartbeat.run.failed`, `heartbeat.runner.agent_run_failed`, `heartbeat.runner.commitment_run_failed`, `heartbeat.runner.disabled`, `heartbeat.runner.started`, `heartbeat.runner.targeted_run_failed`, `heartbeat.schedule.delay_clamped`, `heartbeat.session.archive_failed`, and `heartbeat.wake.deferred`.

All other logger-backed diagnostic records now use the generic event pattern `openclaw.<category>[.<code.function>].<level>` when safe category/function data exists, falling back to `openclaw.log.record` only when no safe logger/category source is available. Subsystem logs now carry the original emitting call site into diagnostics instead of the subsystem file sink wrapper. If an ordinary diagnostic log uses an event beginning with `security.`, its top-level OTEL event name is prefixed as `openclaw.diagnostic.security.*` so only trusted `security.event` records can occupy the `openclaw.security.*` namespace.

Trusted security log actions currently include `security.audit.completed`, `plugin.installed`, `plugin.updated`, `plugin.audit.failed`, `gateway.auth.succeeded`, `gateway.auth.failed`, `tool.execution.blocked`, `exec.approval.requested`, `exec.approval.approved`, `exec.approval.denied`, `device.pairing.denied`, `device.pairing.approved`, `device.pairing.rejected`, `device.pairing.removed`, `device.token.rotation_denied`, `device.token.rotated`, `device.token.revocation_denied`, `device.token.revoked`, `device.role.removed`, and `device.role.removal_denied`.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Redacted `log.record` exports include `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=log.record`, `openclaw.log.event`, `openclaw.log.category`, `openclaw.log.outcome`, `openclaw.log.reason`, and `openclaw.log.site_id` while keeping the body as `[message redacted]`.
- Capture-enabled `log.record` exports keep the same event identity and semantic attributes while replacing only the body with the log message. This mode was used only to prove conditional body behavior; it is not required or recommended for normal operation.
- Trusted `security.event` exports include `eventName=openclaw.security.<action>`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=security.event`, `body=openclaw.security.event`, and the existing `openclaw.security.*` fields.
- Logger tests prove module and plugin/feature child loggers become diagnostic categories with `openclaw.log.category_source`, while generic structured payload fields such as `name` cannot override logger binding categories.
- Subsystem logger tests prove two calls through the same subsystem produce different `openclaw.log.site_id` values from their original source functions, not from the file sink wrapper, and that the trusted source marker is stripped before file output.
- Exporter tests prove ordinary diagnostic logs cannot spoof the trusted `openclaw.security.*` event-name namespace.
- The inventory audit keeps broad OpenClaw logger coverage visible and fails if the production logger/security-event surface drops below the enumerated counts.

Sanitized live local Gateway proof used isolated temp config, fake shared auth token, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`, `diagnostics-otel`, and stdout JSONL log export. Raw temp paths, trace IDs, event IDs, ports, session/account IDs, and token values are intentionally omitted here.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior:

- `src/logging/diagnostic-log-site-inventory.test.ts` enumerates the current production logger/security-event surface and guards the broad source census.

target.title: fix(tui): respect queue mode in sendMessage busy guard
target.body:
Fixes #89059
Fixes #90012

## Summary

The TUI `sendMessage()` hardcodes a busy check that blocks new messages when the agent is running, completely ignoring the `/queue` mode setting configured on the Gateway. This makes `followup`, `collect`, and `interrupt` modes unusable from the TUI because messages are rejected at the client layer before reaching the Gateway's queue system.

## Changes

**Gateway session row** (`session-utils.types.ts`, `session-utils.ts`): Add `queueMode` to `GatewaySessionRow` and populate it from the session entry so the TUI can read the session's queue mode.

**TUI types** (`tui-types.ts`, `tui-backend.ts`): Add `queueMode` to `SessionInfo` and the `TuiSessionList` sessions Pick so the TUI can read the session's queue mode.

**TUI session propagation** (`tui-session-actions.ts`): Propagate `queueMode` from the session entry to `state.sessionInfo` during `applySessionInfo`.

**TUI busy guard** (`tui-command-handlers.ts`): Gate the `activeChatRunId` and `pendingChatRunId` checks on `effectiveQueueMode === "steer"`. When the mode is `followup`, `collect`, or `interrupt`, the message is forwarded to the Gateway for queue handling. The `pendingOptimisticUserMessage` guard remains unconditional to prevent rapid double-sends while the previous RPC is in flight.

**Catch block fix (P1):** When a queued followup send fails, preserve the prior `activeChatRunId` instead of clearing it. A failed enqueue should not forget the still-running active turn.

**Typed-submit gate** (`tui.ts`): Update `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` to accept and honor `queueMode`. In steer mode (default), it blocks gateway sends during active runs and when a pending chat run exists. In non-steer modes, only `pendingOptimisticUserMessage` blocks.

**Tests**: 9 new tests: 5 for `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` (followup/collect/interrupt allow, steer blocks, pendingOptimistic still blocks in followup), and 4 for the command-handler busy guard (followup allows, pendingOptimistic blocks in followup, queued send failure preserves active run, non-queued failure clears active run).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: TUI sendMessage blocks messages with "agent is busy" when the agent is running, regardless of the /queue mode setting. followup, collect, and interrupt modes never reach the Gateway. Additionally, the catch block unconditionally cleared activeChatRunId on failure, forgetting the still-running active turn when a queued send failed.
Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v22.19, OpenClaw built from patched source at commit a1addc94c0.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Type check, lint, and run tests:

Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 2.9s on 9 files with 242 rules using 1 threads.
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/tui.test.ts src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts (73 tests) 25ms
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui.test.ts (68 tests) 18ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Step 2. Build and verify fix in compiled production code:

```console
$ pnpm build
[build-all] phase timings: total 77.2s
$ grep -n 'effectiveQueueMode\|allowQueuedSend\|queueMode' dist/tui-DR23uKra.js

2471:if (!isBtw && (state.pendingOptimisticUserMessage || !allowQueuedSend && (state.pendingChatRunId || opts.local !== true && state.activeChatRunId))) {
3589:if (entry?.queueMode !== void 0) next.queueMode = entry.queueMode;

```

Step 3. Start gateway to confirm module loads cleanly:

```console

```

Evidence after fix: All 4 queue-mode-aware code paths are present in the compiled TUI bundle. The gateway starts and shuts down cleanly with the patched code. All 141 tests pass (including 9 new queue-mode tests), zero lint errors.
Observed result after fix: The production `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` gate correctly allows typed messages through in non-steer queue modes (followup, collect, interrupt) while still blocking in steer mode. The catch block preserves `activeChatRunId` when a queued send fails. The compiled dist confirms the fix shipped.
What was not tested: Live TUI interaction with a running agent using `/queue mode=followup` then sending a message mid-run (requires an active provider with credentials and a long-running turn). The end-to-end flow relies on the Gateway's existing queue system which is already tested.

Fixes #95279

## 2026-07-01 current main refresh

- Replayed the branch onto current `origin/main` with `daily_fix.sh sync-main`, resolving conflicts in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts` and `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.ts`.
- Conflict resolution preserves both current-main ownership metadata (`senderIsOwner` stored under `__openclaw`) and this PR's trusted inbound-decoration contract (`inboundDecorated` / `bareBody`). The `before_message_write` redaction boundary still drops trusted inbound fields when hook output rewrites `content`, while preserving safe metadata such as `idempotencyKey` and `senderIsOwner`.
- After replay, `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` reported `has_conflicts=false` and `sync_main_required=false`; main had advanced by one unrelated skill-file commit with no overlap.
- Fresh current-head validation passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-core.tsbuildinfo`, the focused Vitest command covering transcript/UI/CLI/memory/LLM replay consumers, and `git diff --check` all exited 0.

Added a regression test covering `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }`.
- Fixed the current ClawSweeper P1 type blocker: `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` now accepts any message-like object (`object | null | undefined`) and defensively reads the runtime-attached trusted fields, which removes the `TS2559` failures at the LLM-boundary and CLI imported-history call sites without requiring unsafe call-site casts. (An earlier attempt used a generic `<T extends object>`; that tripped `no-unnecessary-type-parameters` in `check-lint`, so the parameter is a plain `object`.)

No cross-package import is added, so the memory-host-sdk private-package contract surface is unchanged (the `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-b` boundary check passes).

## Summary

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type literal metadata-looking text should not lose that text from the control UI, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory session corpus, or model historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.

  "hasInboundDecorated": false
}

Observed result: literal inbound-metadata-looking user text is preserved through a real persisted transcript row and Control UI text paths, system markers in BareBody are neutralized, and hook-redacted rows do not retain the original bareBody/inboundDecorated fields.
```

CLI imported-session dedupe proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-cli-dedupe-proof-harness>

{
  "mergedCount": 2,
  "preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies": true,
  "wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent": true,
  "bareBodies": [
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal first user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve first",
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal second user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve second"
  ]
}

Observed result: the CLI merge path kept both rows because trusted bare bodies differ, even though both rows had the same decorated model-facing content and would have collided if dedupe still used only forgeable sentinel-stripped content.
```

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`, `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`, `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts`, `ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Each consumer test covers a decorated inbound turn whose trusted bare body contains sentinel-shaped user text such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` plus fenced JSON; the expected behavior is that the trusted bare body is preserved literally instead of being parsed and stripped as metadata. The CLI imported-session test additionally proves two messages with identical decorated `content` but different trusted `bareBody` values do not dedupe into one row.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** It locks the shared trusted-contract behavior at the persistence, UI, CLI dedupe, memory, and LLM replay boundaries without removing the legacy sentinel fallback or asserting unrelated prompt-construction details.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The parser/contract boundary was wrong: `buildInboundUserContextPrefix(...)` creates inbound metadata as plaintext blocks for model-facing prompts, and consumers such as UI history normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export, and LLM historical replay had no trusted way to distinguish host-added decoration from user-authored text in the same `content` channel.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The source-of-truth decision is no longer derived from forgeable `content` text. Consumers now use the shared trusted resolver and only accept `bareBody` when the message/context is explicitly marked `inboundDecorated: true` / `InboundDecorated: true`, so sentinel parsing remains only a legacy compatibility path.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for a public/data-format contract bug.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The change is additive, keeps legacy fallback behavior, and has targeted regression coverage for the affected consumer paths.
- **Patch quality notes:** Dynamic `as unknown` casts stay at existing message-union boundaries where `AgentMessage` can carry additive metadata; guard/default returns preserve existing fallback behavior; the multi-file diff follows the shared consumer contract boundary and is not a downstream masking workaround.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata (`inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody`, mirrored as `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody` on inbound context). Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers use that trusted contract when present and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## What Problem This Solves

Inbound context decoration is host-generated, but the decorated copy can live as text inside user-controlled user message content. Several consumers stripped or compared that decoration by matching forgeable sentinel strings such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` and fenced JSON. If a user typed the same shape intentionally, downstream display/history/dedupe/memory paths could drop real user text or collapse distinct imported messages.

This PR gives consumers a trusted, out-of-band contract for decorated inbound turns: a message/context marker that says the content may be decorated, plus the host-authored bare body to render/replay/index/dedupe.

## Source-of-truth boundary

The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata:

- runtime/persisted user messages: `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`
- inbound context: `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`

The model-facing prompt may still carry inbound context for the active turn. Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers should use the trusted bare body when present, and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields:
  - `inboundDecorated: true` / `bareBody` on persisted/runtime user messages.
  - `InboundDecorated` / `BareBody` on inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body on decorated user turns, while respecting `before_message_write` hooks as the redaction boundary: if a hook replaces content without returning trusted fields, the original `bareBody` / `inboundDecorated` is dropped.
- Update UI display, UI text extraction/export/search, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session indexing, and LLM historical replay to prefer the trusted bare body before falling back to legacy sentinel stripping.
- Keep existing `stripInboundMetadata(...)` behavior for old transcripts that do not carry the trusted fields.

## Scope boundary

In scope: contract/type plumbing for inbound user turns, transcript persistence/runtime merge preservation, UI display normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export/indexing, LLM historical replay normalization, and regression tests for those paths.

Out of scope: removing legacy sentinel stripping for already-persisted rows, changing active-turn model prompt construction, migrating existing transcript files, or doing a broad plugin SDK redesign beyond optional trusted fields.

## Related PR scan

The daily-fix related open PR scan found related PR #94419 as advisory background only. This PR does not depend on that work and keeps the fix scoped to the trusted inbound bare-body contract requested by #95279.

## Review findings addressed

- RF-001 / RF-004 / RF-007 / RF-008 — fixed in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.merge.ts`: the CLI imported-session comparable-text path now calls `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` for trusted decorated user messages before falling back to legacy sentinel stripping. Regression coverage: `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` verifies two imported/local user turns with identical decorated content but distinct sentinel-shaped trusted bare bodies remain two messages.
- RF-002 / RF-003 — addressed with redacted terminal proof for the CLI imported-session dedupe path. The proof called `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages(...)` with two trusted bare bodies and identical decorated content; output showed `mergedCount: 2`, `preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies: true`, and `wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent: true`.
- RF-005 / RF-006 — addressed by keeping the durable contract explicit and additive: `inboundDecorated` gates trust in `bareBody`, consumers use the shared resolver, legacy unmarked rows keep sentinel fallback behavior, and `before_message_write` remains the redaction boundary by dropping original trusted fields when hooks replace content without returning trusted fields themselves.
- RF-009 — passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` completed successfully with no test failures.
- RF-010 — passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts` completed successfully with no test failures, and the same run was repeated including `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` after the CLI dedupe fix was committed.
- RF-011 — passed: `git diff --check` completed with exit code 0 and no whitespace errors.
- Previous ClawSweeper P1 (`before_message_write` redaction boundary) — fixed in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.ts`: `preparePersistedUserTurnMessageForTranscriptWrite(...)` now detects when a `before_message_write` hook rewrites the message `content` (the common `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }` spread pattern). When the hook's returned `content` differs from the incoming `content`, the persisted turn drops the original trusted `bareBody` and `inboundDecorated`, so downstream UI/replay/memory consumers can no longer trust text the hook meant to redact; idempotency keys are still preserved. Regression coverage: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` adds a case where a redaction hook returns `{ ...message, content: "[redacted by hook]" }` against a decorated secret prompt and asserts the persisted row has neither `bareBody` nor `inboundDecorated`.
- Previous ClawSweeper P1 (`BareBody` sanitizer) — fixed in `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context.ts`: `BareBody` now uses the same inbound system-marker neutralization path as `RawBody` / `CommandBody` instead of newline-only trusted normalization. Regression coverage: `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts` asserts `[System Message]` and line-leading `System:` markers are neutralized on `BareBody`.
- Previous ClawSweeper UI extraction finding — fixed in `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.ts`: `extractText(...)` / `extractTextCached(...)` now use the shared `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` path for trusted decorated user messages before legacy sentinel stripping. Regression coverage: `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts` verifies sentinel-shaped user-authored text is preserved for export/search/text-extraction consumers.
